source.title: ScheduleFree+: Scaling Learning-Rate-Free & Schedule-Free Learning to Large Language Models

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares training optimizers and schedules, not the claim’s parameter/token/compute scaling laws or compute-optimal allocation. It does fit and forecast loss within individual training runs, but that does not test the cross-run, power-law scaling versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling ladders comparing ScheduleFree+ with schedule baselines, but these are optimizer comparisons, not tests of loss scaling across model sizes. Figure 12 reports fitted within-run loss curves and a forecast from an early segment; these do not establish the claim’s cross-run scaling-law or downstream-prediction results.
record.test_reason: An optimizer/schedule paper (ScheduleFree+). Its scaling ladders (120M–2B at 20, 100 and 1000 tokens per parameter) compare optimizers at each scale and report no cross-run fit of loss against parameters, tokens or compute. The inverse-square-root fits (Fig. 12) describe loss over steps within a single run, not across scale. No version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Schedule-Free Learning, with their fixes, gives stable anytime LLM training that outperforms WSD and generally linear-decay schedules, with the largest gains for long runs (31% less training time at 1000 tokens per parameter). They report no final-loss advantage at 20–100 tokens per parameter for the largest models. The Polyak variant makes training learning-rate-free, and within-run loss curves follow a predictable 1/sqrt fit.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates optimizer and learning-rate-schedule behavior; it does not apply the original scaling-law method.

fits_no_version.finding: For Schedule-Free training, loss within a run follows a/sqrt(t+b)+c after burn-in. A fit on 10% of a 500M run predicts the rest of that run closely. Fitted asymptotes c are 2.07 (500M) and 1.88 (2B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-run loss under averaging-based (schedule-free) optimizers follows a predictable inverse-square-root decay, so early-run loss forecasts later loss.

record.problems: For the within-run forecasting result, the paper reports no uncertainty estimates and does not test forecasts across independent runs or model sizes. Most loss-curve values are shown in figures rather than tabulated.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. Optimizer and schedule comparisons, including the scaling-ladder experiments, are outside the claim versions because they do not measure scaling-law relationships.

untested.parts: No fit of loss against parameters, tokens or compute across runs.
No extrapolation from small runs to larger runs.
No compute-optimal allocation sweep. Fixed tokens-per-parameter ratios are used only to compare optimizers.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or training regimes.
No comparison of fitted scaling exponents across fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling-ladder comparisons of optimizers across sizes were correctly left out of the rows. The paper mentions batch-size and learning-rate scaling rules and the Chinchilla 20 tokens-per-parameter ratio only as context.

versions.untested_parts: No test of held-out loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute while controlling for bottlenecks.
The forecast is from an early segment of one run to later points in that same run, not from small runs to substantially larger runs.
No compute-budget sweep or loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is tested.
No controlled architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities or training regimes are tested for the claimed scaling form.
No downstream-task performance is measured or predicted.
The paper does not test how scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations vary with fitting choices or setup.

rows.subject: 2B model
rows.operation_detail: Fit an inverse-square-root curve to validation loss over the last 75% of a training run.
rows.measure: Validation loss versus tokens; curve-fit parameters are reported.
rows.note: The paper describes the fit as extremely good outside the initial burn-in period. This is a within-run convergence-curve fit, not a test of the claim’s scaling-law versions.
rows.check: Within-run convergence-curve fit (a/sqrt(t+b)+c) for one 2B run. It is not a cross-scale power law, so it bears on no version. Link and state are correct.

rows.subject: 500M parameter model
rows.operation_detail: Fit an inverse-square-root curve on an early segment and use it to predict the remainder of the same run.

conditions.value: 5% to 15% of the run, after dropping the initial 5% burn-in

rows.measure: Validation loss versus tokens; prediction of later loss from early-run loss values.
rows.value: Fit parameters a = 20.3, b = 377, c = 2.07; the paper describes predicted loss values as near-identical to measured values for the remainder of the run.
rows.note: This forecasts later points within the same run; it does not extrapolate from a smaller run to a larger run.
rows.check: Within-run forecast for one 500M run, from 5–15% of training to the rest of that run. It is not extrapolation from small runs to larger ones, so it does not bear on V2. Link and state are correct.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
